title: Movement Infrastructure Lab: request for proposals (round one)
summary: Open until 30 Nov 2026: pilot call run in partnership with Kickstarting for Good, offering USD 10k development grants from a USD 200k pool for projects that strengthen the farmed animal and food system movements. Selected projects also get founder coaching.
source_title: Why I’m launching a Movement Infrastructure Lab: a request for proposals — EA Forum
notes: Primary source for the existing record call-movement-infrastructure-lab-kickstarting-for-good-2026, which cited Hive only. The post says "Apply by November 30" without a year; 2026 follows from the post date. Hive Highlights of 2026-11-11 reports the pool is now USD 210,000 after Stray Dog Institute added USD 10,000. The call is coordinated by an individual with Kickstarting for Good funding and support, not by a separate organisation. Read on the EA Forum bot mirror (forum-bots.effectivealtruism.org), which serves the same post as forum.effectivealtruism.org.

title: BluePerch: expressions of interest ahead of grant applications in mid-2027
summary: BluePerch invites grantseekers to register an expression of interest; public, rolling grant applications are planned to open in mid-2027. It expects most grants to be about USD 5,000-100,000 for farmed animal advocacy projects. Registering does not affect the chance of funding.
source_title: BluePerch · Funding for high-impact farmed animal advocacy projects
notes: Primary source for the existing record call-blueperch-expressions-of-interest, which cited Hive only. No deadline: the expression-of-interest form is open; applications themselves are not yet open. The fund says its timelines are subject to change. Grant range and first-year budget (about USD 1.2 million in 2027) are from https://www.blueperch.org/about. event_date is the month Hive first reported the fund (issue of 2026-09-23); the site gives no launch date.

title: Who Let The Docs Out: 2026 autumn grant cycle
summary: Documentary grant cycle: pre-applications opened 16 Oct 2026 and closed 13 Nov 2026; full applications from invited filmmakers are due 1 Jan 2027, with notification in early February. Grantees commit to monthly check-ins from February to April.
source_title: Grant Cycles — Who Let The Docs Out
notes: Primary source for the existing record call-who-let-the-docs-out-documentary-fund, which cited Hive only. Closed to new applicants as of 2026-11-19: the deadline given is the pre-application deadline. The page lists weekdays and dates without years for this cycle; years follow from the cycle name and the weekdays. Grant sizes were not found on the page (Hive reported up to USD 50,000 per production stage).

title: Who Let The Docs Out: 2027 spring grant cycle
summary: Forthcoming documentary grant cycle: pre-applications open in mid to late February 2027, pre-application deadline 19 March 2027, full applications due 30 April 2027, notification 28 May 2027.
source_title: Grant Cycles — Who Let The Docs Out
notes: Not yet open as of 2026-11-19. The deadline given is the pre-application deadline. The same page lists a 2027 summer cycle (pre-application deadline 16 July 2027). Funds four stages of production; grant sizes not found on the page.

title: Science for Animal Welfare: Small Research Grants
summary: Open: grants of up to £5,000 for research that improves understanding of the welfare of farmed, companion, laboratory, captive wild or human-affected free-living animals. Applicants from anywhere in the world; closing date shown 1 April 2027.
source_title: Small Research Grants - Science for Animal Welfare
notes: Page last modified 2026-10-23; the opening date is not stated, so event_date is the year only. Research on farmed animals in transport, at markets or at slaughter is referred to the Humane Slaughter Association. Not aquatic-specific.

title: Science for Animal Welfare: Large Research Grants
summary: Open: grants of over £5,000 for animal welfare research projects, with two deadlines a year (1 April and 1 October); the next closing date shown is 1 April 2027. Applicants from anywhere in the world with expertise in animal welfare science.
source_title: Large Research Grants - Science for Animal Welfare
notes: Page last modified 2026-10-23; the opening date is not stated, so event_date is the year only. No upper limit was read on the page. Not aquatic-specific.

title: Culture & Animals Foundation: 2027 grant cycle
summary: Forthcoming: proposals accepted from 4 to 17 January 2027, or until 200 applications are received. Grants of up to USD 5,000 to scholars and artists in any country for research, creative work or performance on human-animal relationships and animal rights.
source_title: Grant Essential Information – Culture & Animals Foundation
notes: Not yet open as of 2026-11-19. The window closes early if the cap of 200 applications is reached. Applicants are notified by mid-March. Grants go to individuals, not institutions. Its feed carried "Get Ready for the 2027 Grant Application Period!" on 2026-11-05.

title: FHF: risk-reducing measures at low oxygen levels in open sea cages
summary: Open until 4 Dec 2026 (14:00): FHF offers up to NOK 10 million for research on when adding oxygen to open salmon cages is appropriate or needed to protect fish welfare and production during periods of low oxygen, including guideline thresholds.
source_title: Risikoreduserende tiltak ved lave oksygennivå i åpne merder – FHF
notes: Source is in Norwegian; status shown as "Pågående" (ongoing). "Up to NOK 10 million" is the ceiling for the call, so the amount field is left empty. Industry-funded research call for Norwegian aquaculture, not an advocacy grant.

title: EUPAHW joint call: Shaping the future of animal health and welfare
summary: Closed 30 March 2026 (pre-proposals): transnational call of the European Partnership on Animal Health and Welfare with national funders for research on livestock and aquaculture systems. UK teams were funded by BBSRC or Defra, up to £730,000 full economic cost per project over 36 months.
source_title: Shaping the future of animal health and welfare – UKRI
notes: Closed. Read from UKRI's page for UK applicants; the partnership's own call pages are script-rendered and could not be read. Consortia needed a UK team (for UK funding) and at least two partners from two other co-funding countries; full proposals were by invitation. The £730,000 limit is the UK component only (BBSRC funds 80%). Publication date of the call not found, so event_date is the year only.

title: Aquatic Animal Funding Circle: 2025 round
summary: After the circle's 2025 cycle of co-learning, a request for proposals and joint evaluation, circle members and aligned funders granted over USD 1.5 million to ten organisations working on farmed aquatic animal welfare.
source_title: Aquatic Animal Funding Recommendations — EA Forum
notes: Round total as worded by the source ("over $1.5 million"); the exact total and per-grantee amounts are not published, so the amount field is left empty. Not every funder funded every organisation, and each funder decided independently. Published under the host's former name, Farmed Animal Funders. Crustacean Compassion is among the recommended organisations; the full list was not transcribed. Read on the EA Forum bot mirror.

title: Coefficient Giving: request for proposals for impact-oriented incubators
summary: Reported open: request for proposals for impact-oriented incubators and accelerators, existing or new, with grants expected to last two to three years. Apply by 18 December (2026).
notes: Secondary source only (Hive newsletter, read via its RSS feed). The primary page (coefficientgiving.org/funds/effective-giving-and-careers/request-for-proposals-incubation) returns HTTP 403 to server-side requests. Not animal-specific: the link points to Coefficient Giving's effective giving and careers fund; Hive lists it for animal advocacy incubators. Year of the deadline inferred from the issue date.

title: Animal Legal Defense Fund: small grants for applied research
summary: Reported open: small grants of up to USD 5,000 for applied, advocacy-oriented research combining legal, scientific and policy perspectives, for US-based researchers affiliated with a higher education institution. Apply by 15 December (2026).
notes: Secondary source only (Hive newsletter, read via its RSS feed); Hive links to an application form, and no page on aldf.org describing the programme was found. Year of the deadline inferred from the issue date. Not aquatic-specific.

title: EA Animal Welfare Fund: Animal Law Italia (2024 Q3)
summary: EA Animal Welfare Fund grant to Animal Law Italia (2024 Q3 round): a 1-year project for advancing aquatic animal welfare in Italy and Europe through advocacy and corporate outreach.
notes: From the EA Funds grants database CSV (https://funds.effectivealtruism.org/api/grants); record id recmwRqqfTRQU9PvG, round '2024 Q3'. The database gives a quarter, not an exact date. Currency is not stated per record; EA Funds presents grant sizes in US dollars.

title: EA Animal Welfare Fund: Animal Law Italia (2022 Q3)
summary: EA Animal Welfare Fund grant to Animal Law Italia (2022 Q3 round): a 2-year plan to advance the legal protection of decapod crustaceans in Italy.
notes: From the EA Funds grants database CSV (https://funds.effectivealtruism.org/api/grants); record id recvga70pxRIDKuGn, round '2022 Q3'. The database gives a quarter, not an exact date. Currency is not stated per record; EA Funds presents grant sizes in US dollars. Grantee is written 'Animal Law Italia (ALI)' in this record.
